New STEVE Stuff
Recent updates to the app — newest improvements first.
Find anything with ⌘K. Press ⌘K (or Ctrl-K) anywhere to search across projects, purchase orders, sources, library items, and pages — and run quick actions like New project or New PO — without leaving the keyboard.
Source scorecards. The Sources page now has a Directory / Scorecards toggle that rolls up each source — committed value, lines, paid-to-date, open POs, lead time, late deliveries, and rating.
Submittal Log. A new project page tracks shop drawings, material data, samples, and COM approvals per line item — requested → received → approved — with a four-day review clock and overdue flags.
Invoice Register. Log source invoices against tracker lines; approving an invoice posts its amount, tax, and freight straight onto the item’s payments and recomputes the balance — and voiding it reverses the post.
Owner Statement. A monthly statement to the owner — PO status, a funds-in-trust reconciliation, and the advance funding request — generated from the tracker, invoices, and POs, ready to save as PDF.
Owner Close-Out Binder. Collect warranties, guarantees, maintenance instructions, and flameproof certificates per source, track them to completion, and compile a single Owner handover binder at close-out.
Client sign-off on authorizations. Send a Purchase Authorization for client approval on the new Client Approvals page; the client reviews a read-only document and signs off with a typed signature, moving it Draft → Sent → Approved (or Changes requested).
Reports & analytics. A Reports Overview rolls up budget, committed, and paid across projects (or just the open one) in switchable chart layouts.
A far more powerful Library. The Library now de-duplicates identical products across every PO and spec book (each card shows how many times it's used), adds combined filters (source, project, source, price, tags, has-image, favorites) with sorting, lets you favorite, tag, and drag-drop your own photo onto any product, and opens a full detail view showing every place a product appears. Select cards for bulk actions — favorite, tag, export CSV, or send to Sourcing.
Product research & a Sourcing hub. Every line item in the Procurement Tracker and Preliminary Budget has a Research menu — find alternates, price-check across sources, find a source/manufacturer, and search spec sheets or images. Save findings to an item, then compare them in the new project Sourcing page and push the chosen product back to the line with one click.
Find sources to bid against a spec. In Bid Analysis, a bid package can now pull spec-matched sources automatically — from the item's saved Sourcing findings and an AI search near your budget allowance — so you have real competitors to bid out in a couple of clicks.
Cash-Flow Projection. A new project page that reads the Procurement Tracker and projects, month by month, the funding needed to sustain purchasing — long-lead items first — with your procurement fee billed up front.
A guided Excel import. Import / Export now walks an Excel workbook through a five-step wizard — upload, recognize the tabs, map columns, review, import — and creates the project, its purchase authorizations, a seeded tracker, source POs, and product images from your ai3 estimate template.
Start a project from an existing one. The New Project dialog can copy an existing project's items, prices, lead times, and photos (each copied price flagged Re-quote) while resetting all order numbers, payments, and statuses — pick exactly which categories or items to bring over.
Action-oriented Project Dashboard. The dashboard now leads with what needs attention — long-lead items not yet ordered, items arriving or to expedite this month, and budget-at-risk categories — alongside the financial snapshot.
Receiving stays in sync with the Tracker. Marking an item received in the Procurement Tracker now records it on the Receiving page using the date the status changed, and vice-versa.
Lead times, with a dropdown — and pulled from PAs. The Tracker has a Lead Time field with common preset values, and when a lead time is defined on a Purchase Authorization it flows automatically into the tracker.
Tidier sidebar & clean-up tools. The navigation is grouped into collapsible sections in order of use, and a Clean up deleted data button on the Projects page removes leftover records from projects you've deleted (deleting a project now also clears its data automatically).
Shared item notes. The note on each item is now one shared source across the Procurement Tracker and the Expediting page — both open the same slide-out notes drawer, so a note edited on either page shows on both.
Paste AI keys where you need them. The “Find Alternatives” tool now shows an API-key field right in its panel — paste once and it’s saved for every AI feature. No more hunting for the key in another module.
Import Purchase Orders from PDF. On the Purchase Orders page, use ↑ Import from PDF to have AI read an existing PO and create a new Source PO — manufacturer, ship-to, item, pricing, and terms filled in for review.
Print multiple POs at once. Tick the checkboxes on the Purchase Orders list and choose Print selected POs to print them as one job — one PO per page, ready to save as a single PDF.
Cleaner document fonts. Purchase Orders, PAs, budgets, and specs no longer render in a stray handwriting font — they now use the intended clean typeface everywhere.
Collapsible sidebar. Use the toggle at the top-left of any screen to hide the left navigation and give your work area the full width.
Item photos & tracking links in the Tracker. Each Procurement Tracker line can now carry a product photo (upload or import by URL) and a tracking URL with a one-click Track ↗ link.
Two payments per item + check numbers. Tracker items support up to two payments each, with a check-number field that appears when the payment type is Check.
“Pay Multiple” lump payments. Apply one payment across several items: pick the items, the lowest item # holds the total, and the rest show “see #…” with a violet band tying the group together.
Red “Urgent” status. A new Urgent status for tracker items — tints the row red and is filterable from the status dropdown.
Tighter Tracker columns & Item # on Expediting. The Procurement Tracker is more compact to reduce side-scrolling, and the Expediting schedule now shows the Item # up front.
Opens on Projects. STEVE now lands on the Projects page when it starts, instead of the firm-wide Home dashboard.
Welcome to STEVE
STEVE is ai3's FF&E procurement workspace. It carries a project from its first budget through purchase orders, source payments, and final close-out — with everything stored together in the cloud. This guide explains how the pieces fit together and answers common questions. Use the search box to jump to a topic.
How a project flows through STEVE
  1. Create a project in Projects (optionally starting from an existing one), then click it to open its workspace.
  2. Set a budget with Prelim Budget, or let AI Budget draft one for you.
  3. Source & research items with the Research menu and the Sourcing page — and bid the big lines out in Bid Analysis.
  4. Get spend approved with a Purchase Authorization the client signs off on.
  5. Order from sources by creating Purchase Orders and emailing them out.
  6. Track money, delivery & cash flow in the Procurement Tracker, Receiving, and Cash-Flow Projection.
  7. Reconcile at the end in Close-Out, comparing estimated vs. actual.
What each section does
Projects
Your list of jobs. Create a project here and click it to open its budgets, documents, and tracker.
Project Dashboard
A snapshot of the open project — budget, committed, paid, and outstanding balances at a glance.
Prelim Budget
Build an early FF&E budget by category or area before anything is ordered.
AI Budget
Drafts a starting budget for you from a short description, which you can then refine.
Procurement Tracker
The financial heart of a project: every line item with quantities, prices, deposits, payments made, balance due, lead time, and delivery status. Each item supports up to two payments (with a check-number field), a product photo, an Urgent status, and a Research menu for sourcing.
Sourcing
A research workbench for the project: a queue of items still needing sourcing, with saved findings compared side-by-side (price, lead time, source). Choose a winner and it writes back to the line item. Products sent from the Library land here first.
Specifications
The project's spec book — a per-item record of finishes, dimensions, materials, and product data that feeds POs and the Library.
Cash-Flow Projection
Projects the funding needed month by month to sustain purchasing — long-lead items first — read straight from the tracker, with the procurement fee billed in the first month.
Invoice Register
Log source invoices against tracker lines. Approving an invoice posts its amount, tax, and freight onto the item's payments and recomputes the balance; voiding it reverses the post.
Reports Overview
Rolls up budget, committed, and paid across all projects (or just the open one) in switchable chart layouts.
Owner Statement
A monthly statement to the owner — PO status, a funds-in-trust reconciliation, and the advance funding request — generated from the tracker, invoices, and POs, ready to save as PDF.
Bid Analysis
Put a line item out to competitive bid: capture source bids, find spec-matched sources automatically, compare them, and award with an audit trail when the low bid isn't chosen.
Purchase Authorizations
Client-facing documents that authorize spend before you place orders. Can be imported from a PA PDF, and lead times entered here flow into the tracker.
Client Approvals
Send a Purchase Authorization to the client for sign-off. They review a read-only document and approve with a typed signature, moving it Draft → Sent → Approved (or Changes requested).
Purchase Orders
Create and edit source POs, print or save them as PDF, and email them to the source. You can also import a PO from a PDF, and print several POs at once by selecting them on the list.
Submittal Log
Tracks shop drawings, material data, samples, and COM approvals per line item — requested → received → approved — with a four-day review clock and overdue flags.
Receiving / Expediting
Track deliveries and outstanding items. Receiving stays in sync with the tracker — marking an item received in one updates the other, using the date the status changed.
Credit Card Auth
Generate a credit-card authorization document for sources that need one on file.
Close-Out
Wrap up a project by reconciling estimated vs. actual costs.
Owner Close-Out Binder
Collect warranties, guarantees, maintenance instructions, and flameproof certificates per source, track them to completion, and compile a single Owner handover binder at close-out.
Files
A central place for documents and images attached to the project.
Library
A firm-wide catalog of every product across all projects' POs and spec books, de-duplicated. Filter, favorite, tag, add photos, and reuse a product by sending it to a project's Sourcing page.
Import / Export
A five-step wizard pulls an Excel workbook (the ai3 estimate template) into a project — creating its authorizations, tracker, source POs, and product images — or exports your data.
Sources
Your source directory — contacts, emails, and status used throughout POs and emails. A Directory / Scorecards toggle rolls up each source's committed value, paid-to-date, open POs, lead time, late deliveries, and rating.
How do I…
Find anything fast with ⌘K
Press ⌘K (or Ctrl-K) from any screen — or click Search in the top bar — to open the command palette. Start typing to jump to a project, purchase order (by name or PO number), source, library product, or any page in the current project — and run quick actions like New project or New PO. Use ↑ ↓ to move, ↵ to open, and Esc to close, all without the mouse.
Compare sources with scorecards
Open Sources and use the Directory / Scorecards toggle at the top-right. Scorecards rolls up each source across your projects — committed value, paid-to-date, balance, number of lines and open POs, lead time, a late-delivery count, and the source's rating — sorted by commitment. Search or filter narrows the cards live; the most-active sources show first, and you can search by name to surface sources with no current activity.
Start a new project
Go to Projects and use the New Project button. Fill in the name and details, save, then click the project to open its workspace and the project tools appear in the sidebar.
Build a budget (or have AI draft one)
Open the project, then choose Prelim Budget to enter line items by category yourself, or AI Budget to generate a starting point from a brief description and edit from there.
Import an FF&E Excel workbook
Go to Import / Export and drop in your Excel estimate. A five-step wizard reads every tab, recognizes the ai3 estimate template, and creates the project with its purchase authorizations, a seeded Procurement Tracker, source POs, and product images — with a review step before anything is saved.
Create a purchase order
Open the project and go to Purchase Orders. Create a new PO, choose the source, add the item details, links, delivery, and tax handling. Everything you enter flows into the printed PO and the email.
Email a PO to a source (with the PDF attached)
On the purchase order: 1. click Print / Save PDF and save the PO as a PDF. 2. click ✉ Email — your mail app opens a new message already filled in with the source, subject, and body. 3. drag the saved PDF onto the message and send.

Email links can't carry an attachment on their own, so the quick drag is the one manual step. Your mail app adds your own signature automatically.
Record a deposit or payment (and check numbers)
Open the project's Procurement Tracker and enter the amount paid on the relevant line. Each item holds up to two payments — set the payment type for each, and when you pick Check a check-number field appears beneath it. The balance due and project totals update automatically.
Apply one payment across several items (Pay Multiple)
In the Procurement Tracker, set an item's payment type to Pay Multiple. Pick or type the item numbers the payment covers. The lowest item # holds the full amount; the others show “see #…”, and a violet band ties the group together so it's clear at a glance.
Mark an item Urgent
Click an item's status pill in the Procurement Tracker and choose Urgent (top of the list). The row tints red, and you can filter to just urgent items with the status dropdown above the table.
Research or source an item
Click the Research (magnifier) button on any line in the Procurement Tracker or Preliminary Budget. Choose a tool — find alternates, price-check, find a source, or search spec sheets/images. Save the results you like; they collect on the item. Then open the project's Sourcing page to compare saved findings side-by-side and click Use on item to write the chosen product (name, source, price, lead time) back to the line.
Reuse a product from the Library
Open the Library, find the product (filter or search), and either click it for the detail view or tick its checkbox. Choose Send to Sourcing and pick the destination project — it lands in that project's Sourcing shortlist, where an Assign to item dropdown attaches it to a specific line.
Put a line out to bid & find sources
In Bid Analysis, use Put a line out to bid and pick the item — its budget allowance comes along as the benchmark. Then ✦ Find sources to bid pulls spec-matched competitors (from the item's saved findings and an AI search) that you add as bids in one click, or enter bids manually. Compare and Award; if you don't pick the low bid, STEVE asks for a short rationale and keeps it on the package.
Read the Cash-Flow Projection
Open the project's Cash-Flow Projection. It reads the Procurement Tracker and lays out, month by month, the funds needed to keep purchasing on schedule — ordering long-lead items first — with the procurement fee billed in the first month. Enter accurate lead times in the tracker for the best projection.
Start a project from an existing one
In the New Project dialog, choose Start from an existing project and pick the source. A checklist lets you select which categories or items to copy. STEVE brings over the line structure, prices, lead times, and photos — flagging each copied price Re-quote — and resets all order numbers, payments, and statuses for a clean start.
Clean up data from deleted projects
On the Projects page, click Clean up deleted data. STEVE lists any projects you've deleted that still have leftover records and removes them on confirm (with Undo available). Going forward, deleting a project clears its data automatically.
Import a purchase order from a PDF
On Purchase Orders, click ↑ Import from PDF, paste your AI key if prompted, and drop in an existing PO PDF. AI reads the manufacturer, ship-to, item, pricing, and terms and creates a new Source PO for you to review and save.
Print several POs at once
On the Purchase Orders list, tick the checkbox on each PO you want (or the header box to select all), then click Print selected POs. They print as one job — one PO per page — which you can save as a single PDF from the print dialog.
Where do I paste my AI key?
Anywhere an AI feature runs — AI Budget, the PA and PO Import from PDF tools, the spec helpers, and Find Alternatives — shows a key field right on the screen. Paste it once; it's stored locally in your browser and reused by every AI feature, so you won't be asked again.
Collapse the sidebar for more room
Click the toggle at the top-left of any screen to hide the left navigation and give the work area the full width. Click it again to bring the sidebar back — STEVE remembers your choice.
Edit item notes (shared with Expediting)
Click an item's note (or + add note) in the Procurement Tracker or on the Expediting page to open the slide-out notes drawer. Both pages use the same source, so a note you write in one appears — and stays editable — in the other.
Your data & saving
Everything saves automatically. There's no Save button — changes are written to the cloud as you go.
It's shared. Everyone signed in to the workspace sees the same projects and data, so edits you make are visible to the rest of the team.
Sign-in is required. That's what keeps the data secure and in sync across computers. Images and files you add are stored in the cloud too.
Tips & troubleshooting
Do I need to save my work?
No. STEVE saves to the cloud automatically as you make changes.
The Email button opens Apple Mail instead of Outlook
Email links open whatever app your computer has set as the default mail reader. To use Outlook, open Apple Mail → Settings → General → Default email reader and choose Microsoft Outlook. (The setting lives inside Apple Mail, not in System Settings.)
Why won't the PDF attach itself to the email?
A mail link can prefill the recipient, subject, and message, but it can't attach a file — that's a limitation of email links everywhere. Save the PDF first with Print / Save PDF, then drag it onto the draft after the Email button opens it.
A number looks off or didn't update
Refresh the page — STEVE reloads the latest data from the cloud. If a total still looks wrong, check the underlying line items in the Procurement Tracker, since dashboard figures are built from them.
I don't see the project tools in the sidebar
Those tools (Tracker, budgets, documents) are project-specific. Open a project from the Projects list first and they'll appear under "This Project."
Still stuck? Reach out to the ai3 team for a hand.
